summary: A list of the UCLA Campus Computing Network contacts for ARPANET users, replacing RFC 389. It names the contacts for user relations, ARPA liaison, technical liaison, operations and consulting.

eli5.summary: A who-to-call list for a computer center, with an updated name for each role.

questions: who handled arpanet technical matters at ucla ccn
subtitle: A December 1972 who-to-call list for UCLA Campus Computing Network staff serving ARPANET users.

tldr.problem: ARPANET users of the UCLA Campus Computing Network (CCN) needed to know whom to contact for which kind of problem.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC lists six CCN contacts and then explains which person to call first and which to call once you are using CCN facilities.
tldr.outcome: It updates the earlier list in RFC 389 and shows the staff as of 12 December 1972.

today: RFC 423 updates RFC 389. It is a snapshot of staff and phone numbers in December 1972, not a current directory.

sections.title: CCN Contacts
sections.content:
Barbara B. Noble of UCLA-CCN wrote this on December 12, 1972, addressed to ARPA Network users. It updates RFC 389.

Six numbered contacts are given: initial contact (User Relations, Bob Bell), ARPA liaison (Barbara Noble), network technical liaison (Robert Braden), operations manager (William Tippit), operations, and consulting.
sections.eli5: The sheet names six people or desks at the computer center and how to phone them.

sections.title: Whom to Contact First
sections.content:
For administrative matters and general facility orientation, contact Bob Bell, Head of User Relations. He or Doug Cummings handles things such as charge number applications and funding, and will discuss the facilities and services at CCN.

For network technical matters, contact Robert Braden, Manager of Programming, who handles problems with Network protocol and Network hardware.
sections.eli5: New users call the front desk person first. Questions about the network itself go to the technical manager.

sections.title: Once You Are Using CCN
sections.content:
For programming problems (JCL, compilers, documentation) and any other problem with using CCN, Barbara Noble is the focal point. She will try to solve programming problems and speed up other matters. A consultant or the Head of User Services can also be called.

For operations questions such as schedules and special handling, contact Operations or the Operations Manager.
sections.eli5: After you start, one person is your main helper for problems, and a different desk handles schedules and special requests.

references.text: The earlier CCN liaison list that this RFC updates.
